No classes; module is pure functions + immutable module-level constants.

_cda_pmax_budget repeats the same 4-line pattern twice (compute mass_rel contribution -> _split_variance -> combine mass+theta or mass+rho in quadrature) once for cda and once for p_max, with only the sensitivity constants differing. Minor -- a helper like _axis_budget(mass_rel, theta_rel, rho_rel, shared_fraction) would remove the duplication, but the current form is small and readable; not blocking.

Functions operate only on their own parameters (floats, the local params dict); no reaching into another module's internals beyond the two documented, cited closed forms (cda_frontier_jacobian's formula, reused as a constant expression, not by importing/poking the view object).

mass_kg/rho/theta_R/cda_pin_sigma travel together across only two internal call sites (systematic_budget -> _cda_pmax_budget, -> _braking_traction_budget); too small a footprint (2 sites) to be a clump smell yet -- would reconsider if a third internal caller appears.

The public return type is dict[str, tuple[float, float]] -- a bare 2-tuple for (shared_rel, session_varying_rel) with no field names, in a module whose own sibling types (ParamPrior(mu, sigma), GaussianPrior2) already use a small typed structure for exactly this 'value + uncertainty-like pair' shape. G4 (a separate implementer, per the handoff) must remember index 0=shared, index 1=session-varying by convention alone; a NamedTuple (e.g. AxisBudget(shared_rel, session_varying_rel)) would make the field order self-documenting at the G4 call site and is a low-cost fix consistent with the codebase's existing convention.
systematic_budget(params, *, mass_kg, rho, theta_R, cda_pin_sigma) is 5 params, mostly keyword-only; internal helpers are similarly sized (<=5 params). Within normal range.
Wholly additive new module; nothing existing was touched, so this change introduces no shotgun-surgery risk (a single future change to the nuisance model touches only this one file).
Single, well-scoped reason to change (the nuisance-sensitivity model); no mixing of unrelated responsibilities.
No chained attribute/method traversal; plain dict/float access throughout.

theta_R is accepted as a required kwarg and validated (theta_R <= 0 raises), but its VALUE is never used in the systematic-magnitude computation -- only the fixed D_THETA_R span is used, per the module's own docstring ('Accepted for interface completeness / future per-session theta_R support'). This is a small, disclosed instance of speculative generality (an interface parameter carried for a not-yet-built future use) that sits in some tension with the project's global 'one canonical path; no speculative abstraction' doctrine (references/global-everyone.md, Universal posture). Not severe (one float, validated, not branching complexity) but worth noting rather than silently passing.

Docstrings and inline comments carry real technical content (derivations, source citations, explicit approximation caveats) that matches clean, well-factored code underneath -- the opposite of comments papering over a mess. No comment apologizes for or hides tangled logic.
